extracted.intended_audience: inventors and applicants seeking to file patents or utility models with Brazil's INPI (first-time and repeat applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, filing, following up, and maintaining a patent or utility model application with the Brazilian National Institute of Industrial Property (INPI). Covers required documents, procedural steps, deadlines, fees, and examination criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of patent (PI vs MU)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two types of patent: Invention Patent (PI) and Utility Model Patent (MU).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invention Patent (PI) – for new technologies, whether associated with a product or a process, such as a new engine for a vehicle or a new process to manufacture medicines; Utility Model Patent (MU) – for new forms in objects with practical use, such as utensils and tools, that present enhancements in their use or manufacture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art search before applying
rubrics_metrics.description: Before applying, check whether no one has developed a product similar to your invention or utility model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Searching databases will help you decide whether applying for your patent is worth it or not. INPI may only provide the patent if no one has invented a product or process identical to yours before. See 'How to do patent searches' for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required application documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent application must include a set of specific documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The patent application is composed of the following documents: Specification; Claims; Abstract; Drawings (if any); and Sequence listing (only for applications in the biotechnology field). Download the forms for these documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of fees (GRU) and registration steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees must be paid to INPI following specific steps and using designated codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To pay fees: register at e-INPI; issue and pay the Federal Government Payment Form (GRU) using the code 200 (keep the GRU number because it will be required for the next step); and fill out the online form at the e-Patents system. Check the service costs. See User Guide – Electronic Petitioning for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee discounts eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain applicants are eligible for INPI fee discounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: INPI offers discounts for: Individuals; Micro-enterprises; Individual microentrepreneurs; Small-sized companies; Cooperatives; Education and research institutions; Nonprofit entities; and Public agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical examination criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: INPI performs a technical examination assessing statutory patentability requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical examination: when INPI assesses if the invention or utility model meets the requirements of novelty, inventive step, and industrial application. For more information, access 'My First Patent'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possibility of additional document requests during prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: INPI may request new documents at different steps of processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New documents may be required in each step. Learn more about the processing of your application at 'Follow-up of a Patent Application' and consult the detailed flowchart of a patent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant responsibility for follow-up and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant is solely responsible for monitoring the application progress and meeting deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remember: you are the sole responsible for following up the progress of the application. To avoid missing deadlines: check the Industrial Property Journal (RPI), published every Tuesday; register the number of your application on My Applications (system sending email notices when application moves steps) via the Buscaweb system. Note: My Applications is an additional service and does not replace consultation to the RPI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality period
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are kept confidential for a defined period after filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After applying for your patent, your application is kept confidential for up to 18 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for substantive examination (36-month deadline)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a time limit within which the applicant must request INPI to examine the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You have up to 36 months to request INPI to examine the application (by using code 203 for PI or code 204 for MU). These terms are counted as of the day you applied for the patent, i.e., the date of filing of your application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary opinion option (code 276)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may request a preliminary assessment of patentability before the official examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can request INPI to provide a preliminary opinion (by using code 276) regarding your application, assessing whether it has chances to become a patent, even before the official examination. See more details in the Patent Applicant Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority/expedited examination possibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain cases may qualify for faster examination processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is possible to speed up the examination of your application in some cases. Check if you fit the profile for a priority examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual fees for application and granted patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual fees must be paid during prosecution (after a set month) and maintained if a patent is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You have to pay the annual fees for the application following the 24th month after the date of application. If your patent is granted, you shall also continue to pay the annual fees until the end of the effectiveness of the patent. The application or the patent may be dismissed due to lack of payment of an annual fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term/duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Length of protection granted by INPI for each patent type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your patent is granted by INPI, it shall be valid in Brazil for 20 year if it is an Invention Patent (PI), or 15 years, if it is a Utility Model (MU).

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to published information and copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can request copies or access information already published about their application or others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may request a copy or access any information that has already been published at technological information. 'My first patent' also helps you with that.
